newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: ICI says 2nd half results to be up on 1st.
newsitem.headline: ICI says 2nd half results to be up on 1st.

text.p: Chemical group ICI Australia Ltd said profit for the second half of 1996/97 will be slightly up on the first half if Australia's economy continues at its current pace.
However, ICI managing director Warren Haynes also said there was no firm evidence of a solid economic recovery and current economic performance was very sporadic.

"We can't exactly predict what the next six months is going to be in terms of economic growth, if the much promised economic growth returns that could be an even stronger half," Haynes told reporters at a press conference.
"If it is much as it is at the moment then it will only be a slightly stronger half," Haynes said. He added the second six months was traditionally stronger than the first half.
ICI Australia, which is 62.4 percent owned by Imperial Chemicals Industries Plc, reported a net profit of A$110.7 million for the six months to March 31, compared with A$92.6 million a year earlier.

"It (trading) gets a bit spotty. One month it is up and then the next month it lets you down. So it is still sporadic, it is not of a condition that leads you to say that 'there is a solid recovery underway,'" Haynes said.
ICI reported a 26.7 percent fall in net profit to A$197.1 million for the 12 months ended September 30, 1996.
At 3.00 p.m. (0500 GMT), ICI shares were 31 cents or 2.56 percent up at A$12.40.
